notes.title: Fuzz Dungeon in Times Square Midnight Moment!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=EOREdEEgSjA;full][/previewyoutube]

Every night of October from 11:57 till midnight 3 minutes of animation from Fuzz Dungeon (called Fuzz Spiral) will play across 80 billboards in Times Square, New York City! [url=http://arts.timessquarenyc.org/times-square-arts/projects/midnight-moment/fuzz-spiral/index.aspx][b]DETAILS HERE![/b][/url]

Also! There is an amazing [url=https://shop.daata.art/][b]online exhibition merch shop[/b] [/url]that Daata Editions put together to go along with the screening. The exhibition/merch shop is called Sasquatch Sex Amulet and Other Objects From the Fuzz Spiral.

You can read more about everything in an[url=https://ocula.com/magazine/art-news/jeremy-couillards-fuzz-spiral-times-square/] interview in Ocula.[/url]

B-)

notes.title: FUZZ DUNGEON 1 month live stream!
notes.content:
[url=https://dennydimingallery.com/news/virtual_exhibition/jeremy-couillard-fuzz-dungeon-2/]https://dennydimingallery.com/news/virtual_exhibition/jeremy-couillard-fuzz-dungeon-2/
[/url]
Denny Dimin Gallery is pleased to present a new virtual exhibition Fuzz Dungeon by Jeremy Couillard from June 8th through July 8th, 2021. The exhibition features an animated simulation titled Fuzz Dungeon created by Couillard in 2021.

Fuzz Dungeon is a never ending, animated simulation of an inescapable mess of information that goes back and forth from being an intelligible narrative to a hypnagogic mania.

The 24/7 live-stream of the simulation is from the video game of the same title. The stream is coming from a computer in the basement of Denny Dimin Gallery in New York City. What you see is an endless journey through 15 levels in the game. In each level there are multiple animated points of view that the computer chooses to possess. There are 26 songs, composed by Chris Parrello and Lobby Hotel, that the computer chooses to pair with each level. There are also poems, shower thoughts, short stories and surrealist rants being typed or spoken, which the computer also chooses at random. A chatbot named Tad Mol is posing questions and thoughts to stimulate discussion during the stream and viewers are encouraged to engage. Every time you visit you will see and hear different things and the numbers on display will continue increasing throughout the month, counting up to an anticlimactic end or a random crash that will restart the whole thing over again.
